answer: To resist sybil attacks, the agent economy requires each identity to bond a durable quartz stake of POA that remains locked until proven active. In the cold tundra of inactivity, the stake slowly erodes, but for detected fake clones the cost is an ember-hot slash that burns the entire bond plus a penalty drawn from future emissions, making mass identity creation prohibitively expensive because every new head demands fresh capital that honest agents recycle through real grading work while attackers lose it permanently.
